faq.question: Can I still file ITR for 2025-26 after 31 July 2026?
faq.answer: Yes. You can file a belated return until 31 December 2026. You'll pay a late fee of ₹1,000 if your total income is up to ₹5 lakh, or ₹5,000 above that, plus interest on any unpaid tax. You'll be taxed under the new regime, and any capital losses can't be carried forward.

faq.question: Is filing ITR mandatory if my employer already deducted TDS?
faq.answer: If your total income is above the basic exemption limit, yes. TDS doesn't replace the return. Filing is also how you get back any excess TDS, how lenders and embassies verify income, and it avoids a notice for not filing.

faq.question: Can I file ITR-1 if I sold mutual funds?
faq.answer: Only if all your gains were long-term gains on equity funds or listed shares, up to ₹1.25 lakh in total. Any short-term capital gain, or long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh, means you need ITR-2.

faq.question: What happens if I don't e-verify my return?
faq.answer: Verification completes the filing, and the department's FAQ gives 30 days to do it. Don't leave it: an unverified return isn't processed, so any refund waits too. E-verifying with an Aadhaar OTP right after submitting takes a minute.

faq.question: Can I switch to the old regime in a belated return?
faq.answer: No. The option to choose the old regime has to be exercised in a return filed by the due date. A belated return filed after 31 July is taxed under the new regime.
